- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling >2% from peak), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.4) and model forecasts are rising, check for overconfidence; reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment >0.4 and price >73.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use 7-day rolling average to anchor long-term forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome is below 65 and sentiment is weak, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to compensate for lag.
- Avoid forecasting below 60 unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.5) and recent price is above 70; model often underestimates in low-sentiment environments.
